decomposition.scenario: re-rating to the base value at the model cost of equity

anchor.basis: reported TTM FCF after SBC (2026-09-30) / opening shares

decomposition.semantics: Re-rating scenario at the model's cost of equity, NOT the return at your required return and not the IRR. Base 5-year return split into business growth x multiple change x cash yield (log-additive, exact): (V_T + D_T) / P_0 = (F_T / F_0) * ((V_T / F_T) / (P_0 / F_0)) * ((V_T + D_T) / V_T), where F is per-share FCF after SBC (fallback: NOPAT per share), V_T the base value at the five-year date at the model cost of equity, D_T cumulative base distributions (buybacks or dividends), P_0 today's price. Each factor is annualised as factor^(1/T) - 1, so (1+g)(1+m)(1+c) = 1 + total. It assumes the stock trades at that base value at T (a re-rating to the model's value); base_irr instead holds the cash flows through the terminal value.

index_expected_return.basis: Market return of the framework that sets the model cost of equity: risk-free 4.98% + equity risk premium 4.20%. The +-1pp range reflects equity-premium uncertainty. Supply inputs.index to replace it.

premium_components.basis: one stock instead of a diversified index: company-specific outcomes do not average out
balance sheet strong: leverage, interest coverage, Altman zone and cash runway (financial_strength without the funding signal)
weak roic_durability under a strong grade: returns may not persist

country risk premium above the US base net of the market average already in the index return (exposure-weighted Damodaran CRP 0.00% - market average 0.00%; the same rows as the forecast's cost of equity)

model_cost_of_equity_floor.basis: the engine's own cost of equity for this company (base scenario), on the verdict scale of the IRR

expected_return.hurdle_rule: required return = max(index expected return + sum of permanent-loss premium components (cap 6%), the model's own cost of equity); valuation error widens the marginal band instead; plus the country-risk row (outside the cap)

price_for_hurdle.label: value at your required return
price_for_hurdle.formula: base value with cost of equity = required return (terminal WACC moved by (1 - w) x the change: 1:1 for a forecast case); the base IRR at this price equals the required return

fair_value.label: fair value: base value at the engine's own cost of equity for the company (the executed valuation)
fair_value.semantics: what the base case is worth today at the rate the engine requires of this company for its risk; the verdict is taken at your required return (buy_below_price), which is a choice of yours, not the company's worth

buy_below_price.label: buy-below price for your required return: the price at which the base IRR equals it (value_at_required_return)

ke_scale.scale: cost of equity (the fair value's discount rate): base_irr + the relevering premium
ke_scale.semantics: annual return over the explicit years if the base case happens and the price keeps today's pricing; equals the model cost of equity when the price equals the fair value. Compared only with bars on the same scale (market return + premium, required return + premium), so each margin equals the verdict margin (base_irr - market / hurdle) and never rises with debt at a fixed price; the level itself can (by at most the premium). Leverage is charged once: the premium is on both sides of every comparison

owner_facing_return.semantics: the expected annual return at today's price shown to the owner: the verdict-scale base IRR (premium-free, never rises with debt at a fixed price, the number the verdict compares with the hurdle); when leverage_premium_base > 0 the debt risk is charged in the fair value (Ke includes it), so this return is shown without it (SAME_SCALE)

convergence_return.distributions: reinvested at the market return to the five-year date
convergence_return.formula: ((base value at the five-year date at the model cost of equity + base distributions paid by then, each reinvested at the market return to that date) / price)^(1/years) - 1
convergence_return.assumes: the price converges to the base fair value path (the executed valuation at the model cost of equity) by that date
convergence_return.semantics: convergence return, a separate internal/report field: the base case's annual return if the price converges to the base fair value path by the five-year date, distributions reinvested at the market return so a payer compares with a compounding market. Not the owner-facing expected return (base_irr, today's pricing kept) and not a verdict input. The engine's values sit below prices on average (docs/CHANGELOG 0.13.0), so this level reads low on average; at_buy_below_price is above the return today exactly when the price is above the buy-below price, i.e. when base_irr is below the hurdle

expected_price_path.formula: price x (1 + r)^h, r = base IRR + 0.5 x (market return - base IRR) (verdict-scale IRR)
expected_price_path.semantics: expected price on each anniversary: today's price compounded at the base IRR pulled 50% of the way to the market return; in the 2016-2025 walk-forward even the best simple predictor landed within +-25% of the realized price only about 65% / 50% / 37% of the time at 1 / 3 / 5 years. The rate is a total return (a dividend is paid beside the price). Not a promise, not a target, not a value; it changes no verdict

yearly_at_model_cost_of_equity.semantics: value per share on each date at the engine's own cost of equity for the company (the executed valuation), distributions paid by then shown apart; a dated conditional value of each scenario, not a predicted market price

at_required_return.semantics: scenario values today with every cost of equity at your required return (terminal WACC moved by (1 - w) x the change, 1:1 for a forecast case)

band.rule: required return -/+ (1pp + valuation-error widening {"low": 0.0, "medium": 0.005, "high": 0.01, "unknown": 0.005}), the index range + premium, the bear-loss tolerance -/+ 5pp and, when the forecast applied a computed moat proxy, the values without it; a verdict that changes inside the band is marginal

five_year_at_required_return.assumes: re-rating: the price converges to the value at your required return by that date
five_year_at_required_return.semantics: base-case value at that date discounted at your required return, plus the base-case distributions (buybacks/dividends) paid by then; the change from today assumes the price converges to that value (a re-rating), so its annual rate can differ from the base IRR; a conditional estimate, not a predicted price

yearly_at_required_return.semantics: value per share on each date at your required return, distributions paid by then shown apart; a dated conditional value of each scenario, not a predicted market price

expected_return.semantics: the owner-facing expected annual return is base_irr (owner_facing_return, SAME_SCALE: verdict scale, premium-free, non-increasing in debt at a fixed price); convergence_return (the price converging to the base fair value path by the five-year date, distributions reinvested at the market return) is a separate report field; ke_scale is an internal diagnostic, never shown. IRR = cost of equity at which the scenario value equals today's price, cash flows held fixed, the terminal WACC moving by (1 - w) x the change (w = the case's terminal debt weight, 0 for a forecast case: 1:1, the convention of valuation_tools.implied_cost_of_equity); a conditional return, not a forecast. The fair value is the base value at the model cost of equity (the executed valuation); the value at your required return is the buy-below price, the price at which the base IRR equals the required return, where the verdict and the bear-case margin of safety are measured. The expected price path compounds today's price at the base IRR pulled halfway to the market return (an estimate with its walk-forward accuracy band, not a value). The 14% aspiration is a comparison only.
expected_return.hurdle_basis: mechanical (no accepted override changed it; analyst upgrades never lower it)
